brief: TS Lombard has been more hawkish on the Fed than consensus since November 2025, when most sellside forecasters still expected multiple rate cuts and lower yields. Warsh's first 100 days as Fed chair were messy: he criticized his predecessor's record and challenged the "revealed preference" framework, which caused the market to challenge him back, and his eventual forward guidance tied itself to one data point. A more humble Warsh has since emerged, dropping the "sock puppet" soundbites. Investor doubt that Warsh could hike ahead of the midterms confirmed to TS Lombard that a credibility hike was needed; the Fed then delivered 25bp, read as a low-cost way to restore his credibility. The Fed is now on a quarterly tightening path but signals only one more hike from here. TS Lombard's out-of-consensus November call for labour-market reacceleration stands: if it happens, the firm expects the Fed to hike more than the market expects, since reacceleration would show policy isn't restrictive and AI isn't deflationary or labor-destroying. The note closes bullish on the US economy but flags an unspecified final chart that evokes 2007-style complacency.
